name: No appointment letter but payslips available
expected: Confirms payslips and consistent salary deposits establish valid employer-employee relationship.
prompt: I was never issued a formal appointment letter, but I have 6 months of salary slips and bank credits. Can I claim unpaid wages?
raw_response:
Hello, I understand how stressful it is to face unpaid wages without a formal appointment letter, but your salary slips and bank statements are very strong proof of your employment.

### | Your Situation
You worked for six months without a formal appointment letter, accumulating unpaid wages from your employer. You have reliable documentary evidence in the form of six months of salary slips and corresponding bank credits to establish your employer-employee relationship.

### | Your Legal Position
- Under Section 5 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, wages must be paid before the expiry of the seventh day after the last day of the wage period (or tenth day if more than 1,000 persons are employed), and failure to pay constitutes a statutory violation.
- Under Section 15 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, you have the legal right to apply to the designated Authority for delayed or unpaid wages, and the Authority may award compensation up to ten times the amount unlawfully withheld.
- Under State Shops and Commercial Establishments Acts, commercial and private employers are statutorily mandated to clear all earned wages upon termination, resignation, or during the course of employment within specified timelines ranging from 3 to 15 days.
- Even in the absence of a written appointment letter, continuous performance of services coupled with regular salary credits and payslips establishes a binding implied employment contract enforceable under Indian law.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence, including your six months of salary slips, bank statements reflecting salary credits, and any communication (emails, WhatsApp chats) with your employer regarding your work and pending wages.
2. Send a written demand notice to your employer explicitly detailing the unpaid salary amount and granting a clear period of 15 days to clear the full dues.
3. Appropriate forum: If the employer fails to pay within 15 days, you can approach the Labour Commissioner or file a claim under Section 15 of The Payment of Wages Act before the designated Labour Authority.

### Information I still need from you
1. What is the total unpaid amount (in Indian Rupees) that your employer owes you?
2. Which city or state are you currently working in, as local Shops and Establishments Act rules may apply?

citations.description: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby.

citations.title: Recovery of money due from an employer
citations.description: Where any workman is entitled to receive from the employer any money or any benefit which is capable of being computed in terms of money, the workman may apply to the Labour Court for recovery.
